questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Greta Thunberg's life as a climate activist
A heatwave that shocked scientists
How people can protect their homes from wildfires
Why Canada has such cold winters
questions.why: They ask if scientists have misunderstood climate change after the unexpected heat in Lytton, Canada.

questions.q: According to Sam, what do many young people feel?
options: That climate change is not a real problem
That world leaders are doing a good job
That Greta Thunberg's speech was too negative
That not enough is being done about climate change
questions.why: Sam says her speech reflected young people's feeling that not enough action is being taken.

questions.q: What happened to the town of Lytton in Canada?
options: It was flooded by heavy rain
It was covered in snow in July
It was completely destroyed by a wildfire
Its residents moved away because of the cold
questions.why: Sam says Lytton burned to the ground in a shocking wildfire.

questions.q: What did the Oxford University team's weather models suggest about the Lytton heat?
options: It should have been impossible
It was completely normal for July
It happens every ten years
It was caused by the wildfire
questions.why: Sam says according to their modelling, such extreme heat was impossible, in theory.

questions.q: What did Geert Jan van Oldenborgh expect heatwaves to do before this?
options: Stay exactly the same
Get hotter slowly and steadily
Become less frequent
Jump suddenly every few years
questions.why: He says they thought it was 'a gradual process' but this was 'a huge jump'.

questions.q: By how much were the previous records broken, according to the professor?
options: By less than one degree
By about ten degrees
By four or five degrees
By exactly two degrees
questions.why: He says you suddenly break all your records by four or five degrees.

questions.q: How has this event affected Professor van Oldenborgh?
options: It has made him doubt how well scientists understand heatwaves
It has proved that his earlier predictions were completely correct
It has made him decide to stop studying climate change altogether
It has made him more hopeful about the future of the planet
questions.why: He says it has really shaken their confidence in how well they understand climate change and heatwaves.

questions.q: What point does Sam make by mentioning Canada and Britain near the end?
options: Both countries have strong climate laws
Both countries caused the heatwave
Only hot countries are affected by climate change
Even cold northern countries can have extreme changes
questions.why: Sam says even cold, northern countries like Canada or Britain can experience such extreme changes.
